# ArubaOS-CX — GUI ↔ CLI ↔ SNMP Mapping

Per [`gui-cli-snmp-unification.md`](../../00-architecture/gui-cli-snmp-unification.md): the CLI column is the literal, multi-line command text that must be echoed into the terminal exactly as a human would type it (including entering/exiting the required mode context) — not a paraphrase. Where no SNMP SET path exists, or where a MIB object is `read-write` in source but has no documented working configuration workflow, that's stated plainly rather than inventing one.

AOS-CX is an **immediate-apply** CLI like Cisco/Arista/Huawei (see [overview.md](overview.md)) — every row below applies as typed, with `write memory`/`copy running-config startup-config` as a separate, distinct persist step, and `checkpoint auto <n>` available as an opt-in guarded-apply safety net layered on top (not shown per-row below; see the dedicated Save/checkpoint row).

| GUI Action | CLI as echoed in terminal | SNMP SET (MIB::object, OID) | Read-back / GUI sync source | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Enable port | `interface 1/1/1`<br>`no shutdown` | `IF-MIB::ifAdminStatus.<ifIndex> = up(1)` (`1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.7`) | `show interface 1/1/1` (admin/oper state) or `IF-MIB::ifOperStatus` GET | Standard baseline object, expected reliable per [standard-mibs.md](../../00-architecture/standard-mibs.md). SNMP is the correct fallback only when no live CLI session is open — CLI preferred otherwise per the unification doc. |
| Disable port | `interface 1/1/1`<br>`shutdown` | `IF-MIB::ifAdminStatus.<ifIndex> = down(2)` | Same as above | |
| Set port description | `interface 1/1/1`<br>`description <text>` | `IF-MIB::ifAlias.<ifIndex> = "<text>"` (`1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1.1.18`) | `show interface 1/1/1` or `ifAlias` GET | Standard baseline object. |
| Set port speed/duplex/autoneg | `interface 1/1/1`<br>`speed <mode>` (exact keyword forms not independently confirmed this session — see [cli-reference.md](cli-reference.md)) | `ARUBAWIRED-INTERFACE-MIB::arubaWiredInterfaceAutoneg` / `arubaWiredInterfaceDuplex` / `arubaWiredInterfaceSpeeds` — **confirmed read-write** in vendor MIB source (see [mib-reference.md](mib-reference.md)) | Re-read the same objects via GET, or `show interface 1/1/1` | One of AOS-CX's confirmed enterprise-MIB write paths beyond the standard baseline — genuinely usable as an SNMP fallback for this specific action, unlike most vendors' physical-layer config. |
| Configure access VLAN (PVID) | `interface 1/1/1`<br>`vlan access 10` | **Confirmed, Phase 2 (2026-07-16)**: standard `Q-BRIDGE-MIB::dot1qPvid` (in `dot1qPortVlanTable`) — HPE publishes a dedicated official page, "SNMP write: VLAN write capabilities," consistently present across AOS-CX 10.12–10.14 SNMP/MIB Guide versions (search-summary-sourced, page itself 403'd to direct fetch — see [mib-reference.md](mib-reference.md)). The vendor-native `ARUBAWIRED-PORTVLAN-MIB` equivalents remain confirmed read-only; this is the standard-MIB path instead. | `show vlan 10` or `show interface 1/1/1` | **Genuine SNMP write path**, reversing this row's prior CLI-only guidance. |
| Create/delete a VLAN | `vlan 10` (create, global config) / `no vlan 10` (delete) | **Confirmed, Phase 2**: `Q-BRIDGE-MIB::dot1qVlanStaticRowStatus` (or `ieee8021QBridgeVlanStaticRowStatus`, both names appear across HPE doc versions) — set to `4` (`createAndGo`) to create, `6` (`destroy`) to delete. Standard RowStatus semantics per [`standard-mibs.md`](../../00-architecture/standard-mibs.md). | `show vlan` | **Genuine SNMP write path** — new row added this pass; VLAN creation wasn't previously mapped at all. |
| Configure trunk allowed-VLANs (tagged membership) | `interface 1/1/1`<br>`vlan trunk allowed 10,20` | **Confirmed, Phase 2**: `Q-BRIDGE-MIB::dot1qVlanStaticEgressPorts` — add/remove this port's bit from the VLAN's egress-port bitmask. Same source/confidence tier as the PVID row above. | `show vlan 10` / `show interface 1/1/1` | **Genuine SNMP write path**, reversing this row's prior CLI-only guidance — notably, this is the only vendor in this project where the *trunk allowed-list* action specifically (not just access-VLAN/PVID) has a confirmed SNMP path; every other vendor's trunk-allowed-list row is still ❌/⚠️ in [comparison/snmp-write-support-matrix.md](../../comparison/snmp-write-support-matrix.md). |
| Set trunk native VLAN | `interface 1/1/1`<br>`vlan trunk native 10` | Same `Q-BRIDGE-MIB::dot1qPvid` object as the access-VLAN row above (native/untagged VLAN on a trunk is the same underlying PVID concept) — **confirmed**, Phase 2. | `show interface 1/1/1` | **Genuine SNMP write path.** |
| Enable/select global STP mode | `spanning-tree mode mstp` (or `rpvst`) | Not confirmed — `ARUBAWIRED-MSTP-MIB`'s 11 confirmed read-write objects (see [mib-reference.md](mib-reference.md)) are all per-port or one global BPDU-guard-timeout scalar; none is a global mode selector. Standard `BRIDGE-MIB::dot1dStp*` is read-only baseline. | `show spanning-tree` | **CLI-only** — the mode selector itself has no confirmed SNMP write path even though several per-port MSTP objects now do (see rows below). |
| Enable STP admin-edge (PortFast-equivalent) on a port | `interface 1/1/1`<br>`spanning-tree port-type admin-edge` | **Confirmed, Phase 2 — the single most significant finding of this verification pass**: `ARUBAWIRED-MSTP-MIB::arubaWiredMstpPortAdminEdge` (`TruthValue`, per-port, root `1.3.6.1.4.1.47196.4.1.1.3.13`), first-hand-read directly from vendor MIB source (highest confidence tier). Set `true(1)` for edge-port. **Aruba AOS-CX is the first and only vendor in this entire project with a confirmed SNMP write path for this concept** — every other vendor's equivalent row is still ❌ in [comparison/snmp-write-support-matrix.md](../../comparison/snmp-write-support-matrix.md), and the architecture doc previously stated no vendor has this. | `show spanning-tree interface 1/1/1` | **Genuine, first-hand-confirmed SNMP write path.** |
| Enable BPDU Guard on a port | `interface 1/1/1`<br>`spanning-tree bpdu-guard` | **Confirmed, Phase 2**: `ARUBAWIRED-MSTP-MIB::arubaWiredMstpPortBpduProtection` (`TruthValue`, per-port) — first-hand-read from source. | `show spanning-tree interface 1/1/1 detail` | **Genuine SNMP write path.** |
| Configure BPDU Guard auto-recovery timeout | `spanning-tree bpdu-guard timeout <seconds>` | **Confirmed, Phase 2**: `ARUBAWIRED-MSTP-MIB::arubaWiredMstpBpduGuardTimeout` (`Integer32`, seconds, global scalar — the one non-per-port read-write object in this MIB) | `show spanning-tree` | **Genuine SNMP write path** — new row added this pass. |
| Enable Root Guard on a port | *(CLI keyword not independently confirmed this session — likely `spanning-tree root-guard` or similar, verify against [cli-reference.md](cli-reference.md)/live device)* | **Confirmed, Phase 2**: `ARUBAWIRED-MSTP-MIB::arubaWiredMstpPortRootGuard` (`TruthValue`, per-port) | `show spanning-tree interface 1/1/1 detail` | **Genuine SNMP write path** — new row added this pass; the CLI side of this specific action wasn't independently researched, only the SNMP object (found via direct MIB read). |
| Enable Loop Guard on a port | *(CLI keyword not independently confirmed this session)* | **Confirmed, Phase 2**: `ARUBAWIRED-MSTP-MIB::arubaWiredMstpPortLoopGuard` (`TruthValue`, per-port) | `show spanning-tree interface 1/1/1 detail` | **Genuine SNMP write path** — new row added this pass, same caveat as Root Guard above. |
| Configure LACP port-channel membership | `interface lag 1`<br>(from the member's `interface 1/1/1` context) `lag 1`<br>`interface lag 1`<br>`lacp mode active` | No confirmed SNMP write path — consistent with every other vendor in this project; LACP membership is CLI-only across the board per [comparison/snmp-write-support-matrix.md](../../comparison/snmp-write-support-matrix.md). | `show lacp interfaces` / `show interface lag 1` | **CLI-only.** |
| Enable port security + set max clients | `interface 1/1/1`<br>`port-access port-security enable`<br>`client-limit 4` | `ARUBAWIRED-PORTSECURITY-MIB::arubaWiredPortSecurityEnable` (per-port, **confirmed read-write**) + `arubaWiredClientLimit` (`Unsigned32 (1..64)`, **confirmed read-write**) — root `1.3.6.1.4.1.47196.4.1.1.3.21` | `show port-security interface 1/1/1` or GET the same objects | **Genuine, confirmed SNMP write path** — the broadest confirmed non-baseline write surface of any vendor in this project (see [comparison/snmp-write-support-matrix.md](../../comparison/snmp-write-support-matrix.md)). Unlike Cisco's superficially-similar `CISCO-PORT-SECURITY-MIB` (also `read-write` in source but with **no** documented working SET workflow), Aruba's is directly usable as a real SNMP fallback. |
| Set port-security violation action | `interface 1/1/1`<br>(exact CLI keyword not independently re-verified this session — see [cli-reference.md](cli-reference.md)) | `arubaWiredViolationAction` (`INTEGER {notify(1), shutdown(2)}`, **confirmed read-write**) | `show port-security interface 1/1/1` | Confirmed SNMP write path even where the exact CLI keyword pairing needs live-device confirmation. |
| Save / persist configuration | `copy running-config startup-config` (or alias `write memory`) | `ARUBAWIRED-CONFIG-MIB::arubaWiredConfigurationCopyTable` row creation — `arubaWiredConfigurationCopySourceFileType = runningConfiguration(3)`, `arubaWiredConfigurationCopyDestFileType = startupConfiguration(2)`, driven by `RowStatus` (`createAndGo`) — root `1.3.6.1.4.1.47196.4.1.1.3.20` | Poll the copy-status object until `successful(3)`, or re-issue `show running-config` vs. `show startup-config` diff | **Genuine, confirmed SNMP write path** — same RowStatus-driven shape as Cisco's `CISCO-CONFIG-COPY-MIB`, a legitimate fallback when no CLI session is open. |
| Create a named checkpoint | `copy running-config checkpoint <name>` | Same `arubaWiredConfigurationCopyTable`, with `arubaWiredConfigurationCopyDestFileType = checkpoint(4)` and `arubaWiredConfigurationCheckpointName` set | `show checkpoint` (exact form not independently confirmed — see [cli-reference.md](cli-reference.md)) | This is the AOS-CX-distinctive safety-net feature (see [overview.md](overview.md)) — SignalScope's GUI should surface "checkpoint" as its own concept, not conflate it with plain Save. |
| Restore from a checkpoint | `copy checkpoint <name> running-config` | Same table, source/dest reversed (`sourceFileType = checkpoint(4)`, `destFileType = runningConfiguration(3)`) | `show running-config` post-restore, or a config-drift diff against the pre-restore snapshot | Same RowStatus mechanism as the save/create-checkpoint rows above. |
| Guarded apply with auto-rollback | *(wraps a sequence of ordinary config commands)* `checkpoint auto 10` issued before the change, then a plain `commit`-equivalent confirmation before the timer expires | Not applicable via SNMP — this is a CLI session safety behavior, not a single object write. | `show checkpoint` / re-read affected config after the window closes | Distinct GUI concept from plain Save — see [overview.md](overview.md)'s config-apply model discussion. No SNMP equivalent; this is inherently a live-CLI-session feature. |
| Configure an SNMP community | `snmp-server community <string>` | N/A — configuring the SNMP agent's own access control cannot itself be done via SNMP (same chicken-and-egg limitation as every other vendor in this project). | `show running-config` (SNMP section) | CLI-only by necessity. |
| Configure an SNMPv3 user | `snmpv3 user <user> auth {md5\|sha} auth-pass plaintext <pass> [priv {des\|aes} priv-pass plaintext <pass>] access-level {ro\|rw}` | N/A, same reasoning as above. | `show running-config` (SNMP section) | CLI-only by necessity. |

## Summary for SignalScope's capability matrix

**Updated, Phase 2 verification pass (2026-07-16).** Aruba AOS-CX has, by a wide margin, the **broadest confirmed SNMP write surface of any vendor documented in this project** — a finding that strengthened substantially in this pass, not just at the initial research pass:

- **VLAN configuration is now confirmed writable** via standard `Q-BRIDGE-MIB` (creation, access/PVID, and — uniquely among all seven-plus vendors in this project — trunk allowed-list/tagged membership too), reversing this vendor's prior CLI-only VLAN guidance.
- **STP port-hardening features are now confirmed writable** via `ARUBAWIRED-MSTP-MIB`, first-hand-read from vendor MIB source: edge-port/PortFast-equivalent, BPDU Guard (+ auto-recovery timeout), Root Guard, and Loop Guard. **The edge-port finding is the standout result of this entire verification pass**: Aruba is the only vendor in this project with a confirmed SNMP path for that specific, near-universal switch-management concept.
- Combined with the already-confirmed, fully-read-write `ARUBAWIRED-PORTSECURITY-MIB` and the RowStatus-driven config-copy/checkpoint workflow (`ARUBAWIRED-CONFIG-MIB`), Aruba now has confirmed SNMP write coverage across **five** distinct feature areas (interface physical-layer config, VLAN, STP hardening, port security, config persistence) — no other vendor in this project has confirmed write coverage in more than two.

This puts Aruba in a different category from Cisco, whose superficially similar `CISCO-PORT-SECURITY-MIB` is read-write in the MIB but has **no** documented working SNMP configuration workflow (see [comparison/snmp-write-support-matrix.md](../../comparison/snmp-write-support-matrix.md)) — the distinction matters because SignalScope must never infer "usable SNMP SET path" from MIB access-level declarations alone, per the flagged case in Cisco's own mapping file. Note the confidence-tier distinction within this pass's own findings: the `ARUBAWIRED-MSTP-MIB` objects were **first-hand-read from vendor MIB source** (this project's highest confidence tier); the `Q-BRIDGE-MIB` VLAN-write finding is **search-summary-sourced** from a specifically-titled official HPE page that itself returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch — both are treated as confirmed for this docs tree's purposes, but the former is more thoroughly verified than the latter. LACP membership and the global STP mode selector remain the only CLI-only actions left in this table without a plausible SNMP path even in principle.
